title: Praise of a letter as rational spring and music
english: You have done well indeed with your wonderful letter. It has brought us a rational spring, and in place of swallows it sounds something very musical. I am as one transported by pleasure, admiring everything: the wording, the thought, the harmony, the writer. And I suddenly think I am a Lydian, imitating the Lydians, who, devoted to Dionysus, observed spring only when Dionysus happened to be present among them. But perhaps you will laugh at this, since sophistry plainly blooms in it, and perhaps you will call me a sophist as a reproach. Yet I am not able not to admire beautiful things; even if you keep silence, my good friend, we speak the opposite. But do not, while I seek, give me the task of representing in writing the grief that comes from silence.
